findings.title: StreamSink#finish closes the queue under a producer blocked in emit, killing it with StreamClosedError and dropping the backlog
findings.recommendation: Take @emit_mutex inside finish before closing the queue so an in-progress emit lands, and return the count of discarded queued parts instead of a bare boolean. Preserve the existing lock order (@emit_mutex then @state_mutex).
findings.evidence: Reproduced by /tmp/f03/probe15_final.rb: capacity 4, producer thread status 'sleep' (blocked in push), then after sink.finish the thread is dead with captured == Tamoz::StreamClosedError and sink.size == 4 discarded. /tmp/f03/probe18_lossless.rb shows the intended slow-but-live consumer path is lossless (50/50, contiguous sequences), isolating finish as the trigger. No *_stream_sink_test.rb exists.

findings.title: Drain#close returns nil, so a close that abandons accepted work is indistinguishable from a clean one
findings.recommendation: Have close return outstanding (the value flush already computes at drain.rb:62) after the join, and stop swallowing its own join failure into the same nil as success. No new class; callers that ignore the value are unaffected.
findings.evidence: Reproduced by /tmp/f03/probe9_grace_drop.rb: close(deadline_ms: 50) returned nil after 0.055s with depths + in_flight == 10 and delivered == 0/10. test/concurrency_drain_test.rb:143-157 asserts only elapsed < 5.0, never completeness. DurableRecorder#close discards the flush leftover count.

findings.title: A drained or closed stream's queued backlog is discarded with no counter and no reason tally
findings.recommendation: None beyond F03-REL-01. If finish/close return the discarded count, this property is delivered with no new machinery; closing F03-REL-01 closes this subordinate gap.
findings.evidence: Probe 15 measured sink.size == 4 discarded at finish with no exposed counter; the class exposes only size and closed_reason. Drain delegates accounting to subclasses (drain.rb:10-11) and StreamSink is not a Drain subclass, so no branch of the design owns the counter. No test asserts an abandoned-event count.

findings.title: DeliveryDrainer is a drain that does not use the shared drain base class; 'drain' names two unrelated mechanisms
findings.recommendation: None. The designs are genuinely different (durable SQLite rows with claim/fence/receipt vs in-memory bounded lanes), so the simple path already delivers the property. Record it as a coverage scoping note: F03's 'shared-budget drain base class' claim covers Drain, not every class named drain.
findings.evidence: grep -rn '< Drain' returned exactly two subclasses (Journal, AsyncExporter); delivery_drainer.rb matched only the substring in its own name. It hand-rolls @stopping/serve_loop/drain_once with no bounded queue, mutex/condition pair, flush, or drop ledger. test/delivery_drainer_test.rb -> 10 runs, 50 assertions, 0 failures.

tests_not_run.reason: budget; exercises observability gem surface, not F03 bounds

rejected_leads.lead: Journal#health (recorder_journal.rb:59-71) self-deadlocks by calling lane_depths inside synchronize, since drain.rb:96 documents that lane_depths requires the mutex
rejected_leads.evidence: /tmp/f03/probe10_doublelock.rb and /tmp/f03/probe12.rb: 'synchronize { lane_depths }' returns normally. probe12 separately proves nested synchronize DOES raise ThreadError on this Mutex ('deadlock; recursive locking'), so health must wrap only once. probe11 confirms the shape works both with and without the lock. No finding recorded.

blind_spots: Clock.monotonic not read; assumed monotonic and non-decreasing, which every deadline in flush/close/join_all depends on
SafeText.normalize internals not read; only its observable raise contract was exercised
Graph node emitter call sites past StreamEmitter not traced, so emit frequency relative to capacity is unbounded in this analysis
Observability::Producer and the recorders.rb fanout guarded(UNAVAILABLE_HEALTH) wrapper only skimmed
tamoz-otel's wrapped real exporter not read, so AsyncExporter's deadline_ms: 2000 is unverified as honored
No load/soak test run; bounds proven by construction and unit tests, not by saturation evidence
Test assertions were run once each, not repeated under varied seeds, so timing-sensitive assertions are proven to pass once, not to be stable
